origins.section: A Floor on Risk Turns the Trade Into a Series of NPV Solves
Five Points Show Where Risk Gets Expensive

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-floor: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-floor: ε-constraint ... the floor is in $k, a number planners can read and set; finds unsupported points too | two solves per point (vs. weighted sum: "the weight has no unit a planner can set")
recorded.prompt:q-slack: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-slack: NPVs are whole $k, so two plans with different NPV differ by at least 1, and a slack of 0.5 keeps the first solve's NPV without depending on the solver's last digit.
recorded.prompt:q-price: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-price: The last column is the price of the next step: from the NPV end, $891k more risk removed costs $112k of NPV, $0.13 per dollar of risk. (column header: "NPV given up per $k of risk")
